UPSTREAM: nb/intel/sandybridge/acpi: Add RMRR entry for iGPU The iGPU always needs access to its stolen memory. For proper IOMMU support, we have to make the OS aware of that. UPSTREAM: soc/intel/cannonlake: Disable CpuRatio and SaGv in recovery Disabling CpuRatio UPD for FSP will ensure it does not force a hard reset to set the CPU Flex Ratio at boot. This is important in a recovery mode boot where the SOC will lose power and need to set the flex ratio again. Disabling SaGv makes recovery mode training faster and mirrors the setting that was done on Skylake. Revert "CHROMIUM: Restrict shared memory access" This reverts commit adc28e54eeb5a1d2433e5adb6fa30b8fa349d990. Reason for revert: Broke CTS, see b/123260752 Original change's description: > CHROMIUM: Restrict shared memory access > > Shared memory can under some circumstances, such as through memfd_create(), > be used to execute code. While this means that the system has already > been compromised, restricting it is deemed useful to stop secondary attack > vectors. > > Disable executable shared memory by default to solve the problem. Introduce > kernel parameter shm_exec=[0|1] to make the functionality configurable. > > As a side effect, legitimate means to execute code through SYSV shared memory > are no longer supported if executable shared memory is disabled. > > This code is experimental. If it causes problems, this patch should be > reverted. Alternatively, the kernel can be booted with shm_exec=1 kernel > command line parameter to restore the original behavior. > > BUG=chromium:916146 > TEST=Try to execute code through memfd_create() and /proc/PID/fd/N > > Change-Id: I85cdf840211bb19e2666e65402bd07c9f843ac1a > Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1389795 > Commit-Ready: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> > Tested-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> > Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org> Bug: chromium:916146 Change-Id: Iebc305fe7296a1c4d21103aadced2db9cf95c689 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1435948 Commit-Ready: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Tested-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mattias Nissler <mnissler@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Guenter Roeck <groeck@chromium.org>
